companyDescription: Clinical-stage oncology · onvansertib (PLK1 inhibitor) just posted positive Phase 2 data in first-line RAS-mutated colorectal cancer · nano-cap fighting a license-termination threat from its own drug's originator
priceNote: Self-fetched today (no live-prices.json cache yet). Trading at $0.84, just above the 52-week low ($0.82) and down from a $4.52 high — the stock has been crushed by a recent dilutive $10M raise (priced at $1.05, already underwater) and a license dispute, even as the underlying clinical data has been genuinely positive.
summary: Cardiff Oncology just reported real, positive Phase 2 data: onvansertib + FOLFIRI/bevacizumab hit a confirmed 72.2% objective response rate vs 42.1% for standard-of-care alone in first-line RAS-mutated colorectal cancer, meeting the trial's primary endpoint, and the company completed a successful End-of-Phase 2 FDA meeting to select the Phase 3 dose/regimen. Despite this, the stock trades near its 52-week low because of two very real problems: a going-concern disclosure (cash funds operations only into Q1 2027) that forced a dilutive $10M raise on Jul 15, and — the bigger issue — Nerviano Medical Sciences, the company that originated onvansertib and licenses it to Cardiff, is actively trying to terminate that license over an alleged breach. ⚠️ SURVIVAL: this is not just a cash problem — if Nerviano succeeds, Cardiff loses its only real asset regardless of how good the Phase 2 data is. TD Cowen downgraded specifically on this dispute. The 8-analyst $5.21 average target (+520%) reflects the clinical data; it does not resolve the license risk. Extreme position sizing only.

catalysts.name: Nerviano License Dispute Resolution
catalysts.description: Nerviano Medical Sciences, onvansertib's originator, alleges Cardiff breached its license terms and is moving to terminate the license. Cardiff disagrees and has filed suit. Resolution of this dispute — in either direction — is now arguably the single biggest swing factor for the stock, bigger than the clinical data itself.

catalysts.name: Phase 3 Trial Initiation
catalysts.description: Following the positive Phase 2 data (72.2% vs 42.1% ORR) and a completed End-of-Phase 2 FDA meeting that selected the dose/regimen, Cardiff is planning to initiate a Phase 3 trial in first-line RAS-mutated mCRC — contingent on resolving the license dispute and securing further financing.

risks: ⚠️ SURVIVAL: Cardiff has disclosed substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern — $46.1M cash as of Q1 2026, burning ~$12.3M/quarter, funding operations only into Q1 2027 even after the Jul 15 raise. This is a real, near-term financing risk, not boilerplate.

The Nerviano license termination effort is the single largest risk to this stock — if Nerviano prevails, Cardiff loses rights to onvansertib, its only clinical asset, regardless of how strong the Phase 2 data is. TD Cowen downgraded specifically citing this dispute.

The Jul 15, 2026 registered direct offering priced at $1.05 — the stock now trades below that raise price ($0.84), meaning the most recent institutional buyers are already underwater, a real signal of weak sentiment
Nano-cap ($57.4M) with extreme volatility (52-week range $0.82-$4.52, a 5.5x spread) — thin liquidity and wide spreads are a real execution risk
A Phase 3 trial requires significant capital Cardiff doesn't currently have secured — even a favorable license resolution doesn't guarantee the funding to run the confirmatory trial
